On UPDATE conflict it uses COALESCE(new, existing) so it never overwrites an already-qualified value with a worse one, but it can freely write null for new rows.

sourceRevision.originalProducerDetail: public.graphify_execution_file_membership_v2.code_source_revision, written per-file per-Graphify-execution. Traced via scripts/atlas/apply-current-execution-workspace-bindings-v1.mjs line ~53, which reads this column directly from that table.
sourceRevision.qualificationMechanism: Zod .superRefine() enforces sourceRevision === `sha256:${contentDigest}` -- a structural cross-field content-binding, not just a regex shape check. Any value not exactly equal to the SHA-256 of the admitted content digest fails schema parse.
fullChain: scripts/atlas/apply-current-execution-workspace-bindings-v1.mjs (admission-gated applier, keyed by a snapshotRevision admission file under docs/reports/workspace-source-snapshots/)
sourceRevision.doesNotStopAt: input.sourceRevision -- traced past the immediate function parameter to its schema-level content-digest binding and further back to the Graphify execution table that is the actual origin of the value.

workspaceRevision.originalProducerDetail: workspaceRevisionRecordV1Schema.workspaceRevision is bound via a separate superRefine to `sha256:${sourceManifestDigest}` -- a digest over the SORTED WHOLE-WORKSPACE MANIFEST, a structurally different input than sourceRevision's single-file contentDigest.
workspaceRevision.proof: workspaceRevision === sha256(sorted source manifest digest); sourceRevision === sha256(single file content digest). Two different superRefine constraints over two different inputs at the schema level -- the writer cannot derive one from the other even if it wanted to, since each is independently schema-validated against its own distinct digest.

currentSourceAuthorityAdoption.consumedBy: persistAdmittedSemanticPacketEmbedding() via buildSemanticPacketWriteAdmissionV1() via WorkspaceSourceBindingV1, matching the expected RepositoryIdentityV1 -> admitted workspace/source binding -> exact sourceRevision -> packet writer -> packet revision chain
currentSourceAuthorityAdoption.stableFileIdentityNote: The admitted packet-write path does not reference stableFileId/StableFileIdentityV1 anywhere in its call chain -- it keys purely on sourceRef + sourceRevision + contentDigest. Not inferring a dependency that isn't actually there, per this gate's instruction.

sourceRevisionMissing.detail: semanticPacketWriteAdmissionV1Schema.sourceRevision is required (not optional) and .strict(); a missing field fails Zod .parse().

sourceRevisionMalformed.detail: workspaceRevisionSchema = /^sha256:[a-f0-9]{64}$/; any other shape fails regex match at parse time.

sourceRevisionEqualsWorkspaceZero.detail: 'workspace:0' does not match the sha256: regex.

sourceRevisionEqualsGitSha.detail: A 40-hex-char Git SHA without the sha256: prefix and at the wrong length does not match the regex.

sourceRefHasNoAdmittedBinding.mechanism: buildSemanticPacketWriteAdmissionV1() requires a WorkspaceSourceBindingV1 object as input -- there is no code path that synthesizes one when a binding is absent.
sourceRefHasNoAdmittedBinding.detail: Not independently unit-tested for the 'binding absent' case specifically, but the function signature makes the absent case a caller-side TypeScript compile error, not a runtime fallback.

workspaceRevisionMismatchesBinding.detail: buildSemanticPacketWriteAdmissionV1() throws SEMANTIC_PACKET_WORKSPACE_REVISION_MISMATCH when binding.workspaceRevision !== admittedWorkspaceRevision. Covered by semantic-packet-write-admission-v1.spec.ts::'rejects a binding from a different workspace revision', executed 2026-09-22, PASS.

sourceRevisionMismatchesContentDigest.detail: workspaceSourceBindingV1Schema's superRefine rejects sourceRevision !== sha256:${contentDigest}. Covered by semantic-packet-write-admission-v1.spec.ts::'rejects an invalid binding/content revision relationship', executed 2026-09-22, PASS.

multipleConflictingSourceBindingsExist.detail: apply-current-execution-workspace-bindings-v1.mjs inserts with ON CONFLICT (repo_id, workspace_revision, canonical_source_ref) DO NOTHING -- a second conflicting binding for the same (repo, workspace_revision, source_ref) triple is silently skipped, not rejected with an error and not overwritten. This is a real, distinct behavior from 'fails closed' -- flagged, not glossed over.

latestRowInferenceForbidden.detail: No 'ORDER BY ... LIMIT 1' or similar latest-row-wins pattern exists anywhere in the admitted write chain read in this pass.

identityBoundary.packetKey: Canonical packet identity. Independent of sourceRevision.
identityBoundary.sourceRevision: Exact source-content revision, sha256:<contentDigest>. Bound to a single file's bytes at one point in time.
identityBoundary.workspaceRevision: Admitted workspace snapshot identity, sha256:<sortedManifestDigest>. Independent of sourceRevision -- see workspaceRevision.relationshipToSourceRevision above.
identityBoundary.stableFileId: File lifecycle identity. NOT consumed by the admitted packet-write path (see currentSourceAuthorityAdoption.stableFileIdentityDependency). Still an open design question per this repo's own CANONICAL-IDENTITY-V1 DECISIONS note -- not resolved here.
identityBoundary.treeNodeId: Structural occurrence identity. Not referenced anywhere in the admitted packet-write chain read in this pass.
identityBoundary.symbolVersionId: Symbol manifestation identity. Not referenced anywhere in the admitted packet-write chain read in this pass.
identityBoundary.candidateOrdinal: Execution-local coordinate. Not referenced anywhere in the admitted packet-write chain read in this pass. Confirmed no downstream representation/execution ID feeds back into packet identity in the code paths read.
identityBoundary.representationRevision: Derived representation identity, tracked separately in packetRevision via derivePacketRevisionV1() (packetSchemaRevision: 'atlas-packet-schema-v1') -- not conflated with sourceRevision or workspaceRevision in the admitted path.

liveReadback.note: All 61,718/61,718 live atlas_packets rows have source_revision = NULL. A 20-row bounded sample was pulled for structural inspection but the population count above (a real SELECT count(*), not a sample extrapolation) already fully characterizes the table -- every row is the same state.

bindingJoinCheck.method: LEFT JOIN atlas_workspace_source_bindings ON canonical_source_ref = atlas_packets.source_ref
bindingJoinCheck.note: Fan-out (78,226 > 61,718 total packets) because one source_ref can have bindings from multiple workspace_revision snapshots. A sample of real src/... file packets (not proto: RPC-contract packets, which correctly have no binding since they are not file-backed) all showed binding_exists=false on direct string match. This matches an independent, earlier finding in this same session's parent-atlas-nlp-sidecar-feature-compiler 14.3a work: atlas_packets uses app-relative source_ref (e.g. src/routes/...) while atlas_workspace_source_bindings.canonical_source_ref is repo-root-relative (e.g. sveltekit-frontend/src/routes/...) -- a path-prefix convention mismatch, not necessarily a genuinely absent binding. Prefix+case-fold resolution was shown elsewhere in this repo to recover ~97% of these joins, but that resolution was NOT applied in this pass's literal join -- reporting the literal-match result, not the resolved one, per this gate's read-only/no-repair instruction.

resultRationale: Distinguishing CODE_PATH_PROVEN_DATA_BLOCKED from a code defect per this gate's own instruction: the admitted write path itself (persistAdmittedSemanticPacketEmbedding + its full backward chain to Graphify execution revisions) is CODE_PATH_PROVEN -- correct, tested against a real database, structurally fail-closed. The reason live data is unqualified is NOT a defect in that path; it is that PACKET_WRITER_OWNER_CONFLICT is the more accurate top-level classification: at least 5 other writers (hyperrag-packet-pipeline.ts, packet-materializer-pipeline.ts, canonical-id-hierarchy.ts, promotion-executor.ts, plus ~140 historical scripts) can still create or update atlas_packets rows without going through the qualified admission path, and nothing in the schema or a runtime guard currently prevents them from doing so. Until one canonical owner is enforced (or the others are formally retired/classified as non-authoritative), source_revision qualification cannot be a repo-wide guarantee even though the correct mechanism to produce it already exists and works.
